angles: Design backward from the de-risking speed limit: the 20% weekly turnover cap is also a cap on how fast risk can be cut, so treat the drawdown bound as a race between a correlated sell-off and a slew-rate-limited exit. Size the risk budget on each day from the running drawdown cushion minus the worst plausible loss the current book can suffer during the number of days it would take to de-risk at the allowed daily turnover (estimated from trailing close-to-close covariance of the held weights), so the cushion explicitly prices the lag that the turnover rule creates, rather than assuming instant stop-outs.

Frame allocation as online learning on the probability simplex: each trading day take one bounded mirror-descent step (e.g. exponentiated-gradient on log-growth with an entropy or risk-contribution-equalising regulariser) whose step size is set so the L1 move per day is at most a fixed fraction of the weekly cap; daily trading and the turnover cap then fall out of the step-size choice, the entropy term enforces diversification at every date, and regret bounds against the best constant-rebalanced mix give a principled, parameter-light growth argument instead of a fitted signal.

domains.text: Fisheries harvest control rules: a 'hockey-stick' rule cuts fishing mortality linearly once estimated biomass falls below a precautionary reference point, while TAC stability clauses cap year-to-year catch changes (often +/-15%) and include an override when stock falls below a critical limit; transfers as a drawdown-triggered risk-scaling rule with a rate-of-change cap and a pre-registered emergency exception budget.

Athlete load management in sports science: the acute:chronic workload ratio (e.g. 7-day vs 28-day load) keeps training load within a 'sweet spot' band and limits week-on-week load increases to roughly 10% to avoid injury spikes; transfers as ratcheting exposure asymmetrically (slow ramp-up, fast cut-down) using short-vs-long realised volatility ratios per asset class.
